title: Suresh Kumar v. M/s Bharat Steels
text: The workman, Suresh Kumar, was dismissed from service by M/s Bharat Steels following a domestic enquiry on charges of theft of raw materials. The workman raised an industrial dispute under the Industrial Disputes Act contending that the domestic enquiry was conducted in violation of natural justice. The Labour Court found that the enquiry officer refused to allow the workman to cross-examine the management's key witness, vitiating the enquiry. Where an enquiry is defective, the Labour Court is entitled to independently assess the evidence. On independent assessment, the charges were not proved beyond reasonable doubt. The Labour Court directed reinstatement with 60% back wages. This writ petition by the management is dismissed. The Industrial Disputes Act requires fairness in domestic enquiries. The workman's reinstatement is upheld. The employer shall comply with the reinstatement order and pay back wages as directed.
